text:
maya-cs: Heads up — AcmeRetail (Dedicated) hit a 403 after an SSO token refresh. Customer says inference calls suddenly stopped working while embeddings/rerank still pass. Blocking their release. Repro + logs below. Can someone triage?

maya-cs: Repro (from customer):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhb..." \n  -H "X-Request-ID: req-acme-3829" \n  -H "X-Sso-Scopes: embeddings rerank" \n  https://dedicated-us.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"missing_scope","missing":["inference"]}
```

maya-cs: They pasted a token-claims dump and we can see inference missing from the scopes string: `\"scopes\": \"embeddings rerank\"` (no inference).

alex-ops: Are they going through our ingress/proxy or direct to dedicated gateway?

maya-cs: Through enterprise SSO -> our provisioner -> dedicated. Not direct. We have their provisioner log id: provisioner.log:lookup:3829 (attached).

sam-identity: I pulled the provisioner logs for that ID — looks like during the SSO refresh path the scope list gets normalized incorrectly when the idp returns scopes with a trailing newline / non-breaking space. We trim on `\n` but don't handle NBSP or mixed delimiters.

nina-platform: We saw a similar oddity months ago when some IdPs returned comma-separated scopes vs space-separated. Our parser currently splits by space only, and then we normalize by joining with a single space. If the original string has a trailing carriage return or unusual whitespace, inference can be lost in the token claim canonicalization.

sam-identity: Quick repro I ran: POST to /internal/provisioner/refresh with body `scopes: \"inference\n\"` -> token claims stored as `scopes: \"inference\"` OK, but when the refresh path flows through the legacy SCIM adapter it does `split(' ')` on the header value which collapses multi-whitespace and a trailing NBSP => results `['embeddings', 'rerank']`. Repro script: `python -c "s='inference\u00A0'; print(s.split(' '))"` shows edge case.

alex-ops: Can we get a short-term mitigation? Customer needs a workaround before we fix parser.

nina-platform: Yes — we can add an ingress header rewrite that normalizes scope delimiters (split on `[\n,\s\u00A0]+` and rejoin). Small patch on gateway, hotfixable. Will need a canary.

alex-ops: Alternative immediate workaround for customer: create a new service API key via our Console with explicit inference+embeddings+rerank scopes and use that instead of the SSO-minted token. That should bypass provisioner path.

maya-cs: I'll offer the console-generated key as a temporary workaround (they're ok doing that for now) and request escalation for a fix. Customer asks for ETA.

sam-identity: I filed SSO-4987 to track the parser normalization bug and added repro steps + attached logs. Link: https://redwood.internal/issue/SSO-4987 (internal).

nina-platform: Patch ready as draft — gateway scope-normalize middleware. Can run canary in us-west-2 with 5% traffic. Estimated rollout time: 30-45m (code + canary).

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued: canary-ssn-normalize-1723 (5% traffic) — queued by nina-platform — ETA ~25m.

alex-ops: Once canary is green, let's promote and also add a short-term query in observability to surface any tokens missing `inference` but having embeddings/rerank so we can find other affected tenants.

maya-cs: Thanks — I'll update AcmeRetail: propose console key workaround + ETA ~45m for a canary patch; mark customer severity P1 due to release-blocking. :pray:

sam-identity: I'll also add a migration script to re-issue tokens for tenants we detect as affected (safe re-issue flow, no creds change).

maya-cs: Perfect — keep me posted in this thread and I'll relay to the customer.

nina-platform: Adding a note to postmortem and to our SSO integration docs about whitespace/delimiter normalization.

maya-cs: Appreciate the quick turnaround.
